channel.title: Product Diary
channel.description: What changed across the projects, day by day.

item.title: AI Benchmark Suite Starts Scoring Local Models on Real Tasks
item.description: A new test bench now sets 25 build-it tasks for AI models on my two home machines and scores what they produce, resumes stuck runs and keeps receipts.

item.title: AI Models Site Lists 25 Agent Tasks and Saves Routing Receipts
item.description: The benchmarks page in my local AI model catalog now lists the agent tasks I test models on, with a way to keep a record of each run.

item.title: Bosgame M5 Pair Serves DeepSeek and Strata Stops Swapping
item.description: My two small AI computers now run one huge model together over a single cable, and a memory-hungry setting that made one of them swap is fixed.

item.title: AI Benchmark Suite Scores Local Models as Quiet Links Grows
item.description: I built a bench that scores local AI models on 25 real tasks, paired two Bosgame machines on one huge model, and Quiet Links golf got crowds.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Fixes Shadows That Bled Onto Cutscenes
item.description: The shadows in my Mac version of the PlayStation 3 game no longer smear over the cutscenes, and the first measured frame rates with them on are in.

item.title: Butcher Bay on Mac Adds Mouse Play and PlayStation Buttons
item.description: The Mac port of the Xbox game now plays with mouse and keyboard, shows PlayStation or keyboard buttons on screen, and runs as one self-contained app.

item.title: Quiet Links Golf Gets Real Crowds, Boulders and an iPhone App
item.description: My browser golf game now has mowed stripes, rocks that stop the ball, a crowd built from the golfer, and a first install on my phone.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Log the Second Bosgame M5 Joining the Network
item.description: The notes on my fleet of assistants recorded my second mini AI computer joining the private network, with one machine low on memory and two still missing.

item.title: AI Models Catalog Swaps Six Results for 32 Measured Ones
item.description: The benchmarks page in my local AI model catalog now shows 32 speed results from my own machine, replacing the six it had the day before.

item.title: Bosgame M5 Gets Remote Desktop and 32 Speed Results
item.description: My first mini AI computer can now be controlled from my laptop's screen, and every model on it has a measured speed on two graphics paths.

item.title: Bosgame M5 Gets Real Speeds, Butcher Bay Gets Game Mode
item.description: On 24 November my Bosgame M5 got 32 measured model speeds and remote desktop, and the Mac port of Escape from Butcher Bay switched Game Mode on.

item.title: Dante Audit Host Adds Ray-Traced Shadow Settings
item.description: The cautious Mac build of the PlayStation 3 game gained menu options for ray-traced shadows, but nothing has been committed or tried in play.

item.title: Butcher Bay on Mac Now Switches Game Mode On at Launch
item.description: The Mac port of the Xbox game now draws crisply in a window, goes 4K in full screen, and the Mac recognises it as a game.

item.title: Quiet Links Golf Gets Reflections, Refraction and Pad Test
item.description: My browser golf game now draws the pond's reflections of off-screen trees and bends the pond bed, and a game controller is covered by a test.

item.title: The First Bosgame M5 Boots and Corrects My Runbook
item.description: The first of two small home AI computers was set up from one script and now runs my chat models, though the hardware overruled several of my plans.

item.title: Butcher Bay on Mac Gets Its Missing Floor and a 4K Renderer
item.description: The Mac port of the Xbox game lost its black strip of missing floor in the courtyard, and it now has a new native Apple graphics path that draws at 4K.

item.title: The Grok Bot Wiki Gets a Front Door, Then Goes Private
item.description: My wiki about the fleet of assistants gained search and a visitor guide on Monday, then I took it off the public internet because it describes my home network.

item.title: Butcher Bay Mac Port Gets Debug Tools as M5 Boxes Near
item.description: Sunday I gave my Mac port of Escape from Butcher Bay better ways to chase its dark characters, tested a careful Dante build and wrote an M5 runbook.

item.title: Dante Audit Host Gets a Careful Build That Picks a Difficulty
item.description: My Mac version of a PlayStation 3 game now has a separate, cautious test build that reached the difficulty screen and the opening story.

item.title: Butcher Bay on Mac Gets a Performance Overlay and Debug Views
item.description: The Mac port of the Xbox game now has an Apple performance overlay and a truer frame-rate readout, plus new tools for chasing the dark characters.

item.title: Learning to Sell, Part 2: Four Weeks, No Paid Sales, One Tagged Click
item.description: Four weeks after the first entry, nothing new has sold, ad spend is still zero, and the only tagged sign of life is one SnapDog store click that didn't buy. CyberSim's Full Access purchase is live. Book and StatBar sales are still missing.

item.title: A Runbook for Two Bosgame M5 Mini PCs Before They Arrive
item.description: I wrote a ready-to-run setup guide for two new small Linux computers that will host my local AI models, before either one has been switched on.

item.title: AI Models Catalog Gets a Measured Benchmarks Page
item.description: My local AI model catalog now has a page of real speed measurements, each labelled as reading speed or writing speed with its source.

item.title: Comfy Golf Gets a Landing Page, a Guide and a Playable Demo
item.description: Comfy Golf now has a public website with a how-to-play guide and a demo you can try in the browser without installing anything.

item.title: Butcher Bay Mac Port Hits 60 fps, Comfy Golf Gets a Site
item.description: The Mac port of Escape from Butcher Bay now plays smoothly but draws characters too dark, while Comfy Golf and my AI models catalog gained new pages.

item.title: Butcher Bay on Mac Runs Smooth, but Characters Stay Dark
item.description: The Mac port of the Xbox game now plays smoothly and packages as a real app, but the characters still render too dark.

item.title: Quiet Links Golf Gets a Swing as Dante Recomp Speeds Up
item.description: On Friday my browser golf game Quiet Links gained a three-press swing and a caddie, while three Mac game conversions each moved a little.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Skips Ahead and Gets a Graphics Menu
item.description: My Mac version of a PlayStation 3 game now reaches its first battle 47 seconds sooner and has a graphics settings page inside the game's own menu.

item.title: Eternal Darkness Holds 60 in a Window on My Mac
item.description: A Mac conversion of a GameCube horror game held 60 frames a second in a window, and its new faster-screen option stayed hidden on my fixed screens.

item.title: Quiet Links Golf Gets a Three-Press Swing and a Caddie
item.description: My browser golf game now has a swing you control with three presses, a second course, a caddie and a golfer you can dress yourself.

item.title: GoW3 Recomp Writes Its Handover Note Without an App
item.description: My PlayStation 3 God of War III conversion still stops after its opening splash screen, so I wrote a handover and chose not to package it.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Show a Quiet Day on the New Connector
item.description: The notes on my fleet of assistants recorded a second quiet day on the built-in network connector, plus a new God of War folder and five stray empty ones.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Reports a Golf Build That Does Not Match Its Link
item.description: My house assistant wrote three progress reports on Friday and admitted that the golf preview link served an older build than the code.

item.title: Week of November 13: Silent Tests, a Golfer, a Frozen Splash
item.description: A week of green lights that meant less than they seemed. SnapDog's tests had stopped running, a golf game got its golfer, a PS3 conversion froze on a splash screen, and nothing sold.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Plays on My Mac as GoW3 Recomp Hangs
item.description: A converted PlayStation 3 game reached real gameplay on my Mac while a second, God of War III, drew a splash screen and froze.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Plays From Logo to the First Level
item.description: The converted PlayStation 3 game now starts on my Mac and reaches real gameplay, though an automated tester has not yet got it through a level.

item.title: GoW3 Recomp Draws Its Splash Screen, Then Hangs
item.description: A PlayStation 3 God of War game converted for my Mac reaches its own opening splash screen, then freezes for a reason I have pinned down.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Log the Server Box Switching Connectors
item.description: My server box stopped using a home-built private-network workaround and now uses its built-in connector, which also closed one failed-scan note.

item.title: Build Fleet Guide Explains Why Generated Files Go Missing
item.description: My build fleet's guide now says why folders of generated files never reach another computer, and how to get them there without cheating.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Links Two Programs, Nothing Run Yet
item.description: My PS3 game-conversion experiment finished a Mac build on Wednesday, but I have not launched it, while Grok Bot and Hermes Fleet reported quietly.

item.title: Dante Recomp Host Compiles and Links Two Programs
item.description: A game-conversion experiment finished an 84-step build on the Mac and linked two programs, but nothing has been run yet.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Add Game Guru and Log a Failed Scan
item.description: A new assistant called Game Guru joined my fleet on Tuesday afternoon, but its profile is a name and nothing else, and one overnight scan failed.

item.title: Hermes Fleet Writes Seven Progress Previews on Wednesday
item.description: My house assistant wrote seven short progress reports on Wednesday, while its list of household computers is still a week out of date.

item.title: Golfprompt's Quiet Links Gets a Golfer and Phone Controls
item.description: My browser golf game Quiet Links got a real golfer, a swing that hits the ball and touch controls on Tuesday, while my assistant fleet's notes stayed quiet.

item.title: Quiet Links Golf Game Gets a Real Golfer and Phone Controls
item.description: My browser golf game now has a real golfer who hits the ball, a loading screen, and touch controls that run on a phone instead of crawling.

item.title: Grok Bot Notes Record Tools Returning After a Box Rewrite
item.description: The notes on my fleet of 30 assistants logged no bot changes on Tuesday, but the coding tools missing from the server box were back.

item.title: SnapDog 1.2.2 Goes to Apple Review, Golf Game Gets Built
item.description: SnapDog 1.2.2 went to Apple for review after I restored three fixes an old change had undone, and a one-hole browser golf game appeared overnight.

item.title: Quiet Links Golf Prototype Gets an Honest Missing-Art Card
item.description: A one-hole 3D golf game built in a browser now plays start to finish, and its stand-in golfer has been replaced by a plain warning card.

item.title: SnapDog 1.2.2 Goes to Apple Review With Loom Import
item.description: I sent SnapDog 1.2.2 to Apple for review after restoring three fixes that an old commit had quietly undone.

item.title: SnapDog Tests Revived, App Store Status Corrected
item.description: I got SnapDog's dead test suite running again on Sunday and found its Loom import was never shipped, so nobody outside my machines has it.
